principle: P8.1 · strains P2: "Every clause the mechanism applies subtracts except one: binding a subject at grant, whose authority is the subject's provider's (§2)"
feature: **Confirmation is required under C1, and under C2 for §5.** C1 because "A subject-bound credential is a new route by which an admitted call carries authority that is not the deployment's own (§3, §5)"; C2 because "the tool host's premise widens, and the claim that a tool sees exactly one credential is an exhaustiveness claim on the channel".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056; C1, and C2 for §5); Open (§11: no item is marked met)
note: Deployment position: "Archetype. Three degeneracies (§9)." The record is the archetype's, not an overlay's.

feature: **A user's scope is enforced downstream and is not carried in the lease ⟨U1⟩.** "A per-user credential can only make an admitted call do *less*. It weakens no theorem, and none needs to rest on it"; the subject as a thirteenth lease field is rejected because "Every lease field is authority the mechanism grants (ADR-0031 §1)".
basis: ADR-0056 provenance note; Context; Options considered
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared (settled by the custodian, ⟨U1⟩)

feature: **Which user a call acts for is decided by the mechanism and the policy, not by the model ⟨U2⟩.** "A wrong binding *adds* authority: another user's", so the component that decides it "must be checked, or be a trust root with an issued identity"; "A model is neither, and a tool's behaviour is a claim (ADR-0049 §4). So the binding must be a syntactic lift from something on the record".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared (settled by the custodian, ⟨U2⟩)

feature: **Four questions, four owners.** Which user a round acts for is decided by the mechanism, "Checked at grant"; whether a call may use that user's credential by the policy, "Checked at admit"; what the credential may do downstream by the downstream system, "Outside the pattern, by position"; and which credential the tool presents by "Nobody: the tool host injects the one credential for the round's subject".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056; C1); not built

feature: **The tool decides nothing (drafter's choice; the custodian asked).** A tool that chooses "must hold every subject's credential"; "A tool's behaviour is a claim", so a choice made inside it "is made past the membrane, off the record"; and "Letting the tool choose is letting the model choose, one step removed".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared
note: The provenance note marks this answer as the drafter's and not one of the two things the custodian settled.

feature: **A subject is not a principal (drafter's choice).** "It holds no seat, no lease and no alphabet, and it is not promoted. It is the party whose downstream authority a round's calls may use. ADR-0037's one-seat-per-principal rule is untouched."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared

feature: **A grant may carry at most one subject, beside the lease and not in it.** It is carried "beside the lease and not in it, as the task and its label are (ADR-0050 §5; ADR-0031 A3). §1's lease field set stays closed. A grant carries at most one subject."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built; Open (§11: the entries to ADR-0050 §5 and ADR-0031 A3 are not drafted)

feature: **The evidence is a subject assertion, checked at grant, and its freshness is the fence.** It is "signed by a provider whose key is on the issued rules' list of subject providers (ADR-0025 §1 (f))" and names the subject, the provider and "the fence of the grant it is presented for". "An assertion that does not verify, or names another fence, refuses the grant. No wall clock is read: freshness is the fence."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056; C1); not built; Open (the form of the subject assertion; §11's `SubjectEvidenced` and `M_STALE_ASSERTION` are stated by no module)

feature: **Whoever submits the grant cannot name a subject without that subject's assertion.** "So an operator cannot act as an arbitrary user, and a subject is attributed to its provider's signature rather than to the operator's word."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built

feature: **The seating bounds whether a round may carry a subject (drafter's choice).** "A seating names whether its rounds may carry a subject and from which providers, as it names the labels a task may carry (ADR-0050 §5). A grant outside that bound is refused. A quorum decides that a seat acts for users. One operator cannot."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built

feature: **One subject per round, fixed at grant (drafter's choice).** "A subject cannot be added, changed or dropped inside a round, as the tool list cannot (ADR-0048 §2). A cell that serves two users serves them in two rounds." This keeps each user's content in that user's round topic, "so ADR-0003's unit of erasure stays per principal per round".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built; Open (§11's `SubjectFixedForRound` and `M_RESUBJECT` are stated by no module)

feature: **The subject's authority ends with the round, and an absent user cannot be acted for.** "The lease's `ttl` bounds it (ADR-0031 A2). Nothing is refreshed inside a round. A user who is not present at grant cannot be acted for (finding 2)." Finding 2 calls this "the right failure direction: an absent user's authority lapses", and says it excludes scheduled or long-running work for a user.
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared (finding 2)

feature: **The entry's channel gains a `credential` part, each field checked or claimed.** `channel.credential.mode` (`none`, `service` or `subject`) and `channel.credential.providers` are checked; `channel.credential.scope`, "Text: what the credential permits downstream", is claimed: "What the downstream system enforces is its own".
basis: ADR-0056 §3; ADR-0049 §1, §4 (the dependent amendment is not drafted)
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built; Open (§11: the ADR-0049 entry is not drafted)
note: Negative consequence: "`scope` is a claim, like `purpose`. A reviewer at promotion is told what the credential permits and cannot check it."

feature: **The mode is required and has no default (drafter's choice).** "A Run entry without it does not load", by the totality rule that ADR-0047 §1 and ADR-0049 W4 apply; "A Build entry has no channel, so it has no credential."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built
note: Negative consequence: "Every Run entry changes form (W11): a bundle and policy change together, as ADR-0049's was."

feature: **`service` is permitted, is not the default, and is where LLM06's example 5 survives (finding 3).** "Whether a `service` entry reaches per-user data is a claim nothing checks"; an entry declared `service` that in fact reaches per-user data "is the generic high-privileged identity, and nothing checks the declaration. The `scope` text and promotion are the only defence, as for `purpose`."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared (finding 3)

feature: **Three load checks, W11 to W13, are added to ADR-0049 §6.** The bundle is refused when a Run entry's channel "has no `credential.mode`, or a mode outside the three" (W11); when a `subject` entry "names no provider, or a provider the issued rules do not list, or has empty `scope` text" (W12); and when a `none` or `service` entry "carries `providers`" (W13).
basis: ADR-0056 §3; ADR-0049 §6 (the dependent amendment is not drafted)
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built; Open (§11: the ADR-0049 entry is not drafted)

feature: **The lift adds five attributes, each "a lift from the record, mechanical and total (ADR-0007)".** To `RunCtx`, from the grant: `subject.present`, `subject.provider` and `subject.attributes`, "the claims the provider signed, as a set of names"; to the tool: `credentialMode` and `subjectProviders`.
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built; Open (the size and form of `subject.attributes`, and which provider claims may be lifted)

feature: **The floor carries a minimum of two forbids on `Actuate`, `R10` and `R11`.** `R10-subject-entry-needs-subject` holds when "the tool's `credentialMode` is `subject` and `subject.present` is false"; `R11-subject-provider-accepted` when "the tool's `credentialMode` is `subject` and `subject.provider` is not in the tool's `subjectProviders`", and it "duplicates what the tool host would fail anyway, and is kept so the refusal is an admit decision on the record".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built (`floor/proposed/` has no `subjects` stage); Open (§11: the stage "validated, tested and gated, each entry shown to fire and none shown vacuous")
note: §4: "The ids take the next free numbers after the `workflow` stage's `R8` and `R9`" (drafter's choice). That stage is Proposed and not in force (`floor/proposed/workflow-floor.cedar` opened: `R8-route-own-decision`, `R9-only-orchestrators-route`), while §11 builds `subjects` "on the stage in force when this is ratified".

feature: **The bundle may narrow on `subject.attributes`, and a provider's claim can only subtract.** "By `bundle ⊑ floor` such a rule can only deny more. A provider's claim can therefore subtract authority, and never add it."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built

feature: **No floor entry looks for a subject in the inputs.** "Telling whether a free-text input names a user is a judgment. §6 closes the path downstream instead." Marking a subject input as a `destination`, so that F2 and F3 apply, is not taken: "It stretches what a destination is, and it still lets a Thinker that has read only trusted content name any user".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared

feature: **The tool host injects the one credential, and the tool has no means to obtain another.** At each `Actuate` on a `subject` entry "the tool host obtains the credential for the round's subject and presents it on the tool's one channel"; "The tool receives exactly that credential and no means to obtain another. For `service`, the host injects the entry's service credential. For `none`, nothing."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056; C2); not built; Open (§11's `InjectedIsRoundSubject` and `M_INPUT_SUBJECT` are stated by no module)

feature: **The preferred form is exchange, not storage (drafter's choice).** "The host exchanges the round's subject assertion for a downstream credential scoped to that subject, so no standing credential for any user exists at rest in the deployment. A store of per-user credentials that the host selects from is D-0056-2."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared (a preference; the other form is a declared degeneracy)

feature: **Neither the assertion nor the credential is ingress, and the tool list does not show the subject.** "The Listener never delivers them. They are not in the round payload a Thinker reads, and they are not in any record's payload." The tool list shows each entry's `credential.mode` and `scope`, "so a Thinker knows a call acts as its user. It does not show the subject. The task may name the user, and that is content."
basis: ADR-0056 §5; §7; ADR-0048 §2 (the dependent amendment is not drafted)
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built; Open (§11: the ADR-0048 §2 entry is not drafted)
note: Two sentences of the record stand against each other and it does not say how they differ: §5 has the assertion not "in any record's payload"; §7 has "The assertion's bytes are in the round's payload, inside the unit of erasure (ADR-0003)."

feature: **An assumption of use carries the weight for free text.** A downstream system that a `subject` entry reaches "authorizes on the subject its credential names, and never on a subject named in the request"; finding 5: "§6 is an assumption, and it carries the weight for free text. The floor cannot find a user named in an input."
basis: ADR-0056 §6; finding 5; ToO §13 (the dependent amendment is not drafted)
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared (an assumption of use)

feature: **The grant record carries the subject's provider and a digest of the subject's identifier (drafter's choice).** "This is an authority fact, so it is in the forensic floor and survives erasure (ADR-0028). The assertion's bytes are in the round's payload, inside the unit of erasure (ADR-0003)." Every `Actuate` record on a `subject` entry is attributable to the subject through its round's grant, and "The admit record gains no field."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built; Open (whether a digest of a personal identifier in the forensic floor meets a deployment's data obligations)

feature: **An Observer and the correlator read the subject's digest.** They read it "as they read every grant fact, so a finding can name the user a round acted for".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built

feature: **T-0045-38: a subject provider is a trust root whose identity is issued.** Its failure can produce "A round that acts for a subject who did not ask, within what the seating and floor allow"; "A provider is a trust root for the subjects it vouches for, and for no others, as an operator's provider is (T-0045-35). One provider may serve both."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056; C1); Declared; Open (§11: the entries to ADR-0045 and ADR-0025 A2 are not drafted)
note: ADR-0045 has no T-0045-38 or T-0045-39 at bbda621. The two ids occur only in ADR-0056, `diagrams/README.md` and the C10 diagram.

feature: **T-0045-25 is widened: the tool host is also trusted to present only the round's subject's credential.** "The tool host already runs only the allowlisted binary and binds its socket (ADR-0034 A2). It is now also trusted to present only the round's subject's credential." Its failure can now also produce "a call presented with another subject's credential".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056; C2); Declared; Open (§11: the entries to ADR-0042 §6 and ADR-0045 are not drafted)

feature: **T-0045-39, a downstream system's authorization, is excluded, "and that is the position, not a gap".** "Every theorem stays about the membrane. The row exists so that a reader computing a deployment's guarantees sees that per-user scope is the downstream system's." The row also covers "any token service that mints for it".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared
note: Negative consequence: "T-0045-39 is a row that admits the pattern does not reach the scope."

feature: **D-0056-1, a declared subject.** "the subject is named by the operator's signed grant, with no provider assertion"; "Attribution moves from the subject's provider to the operator. A havoc operator can act for any subject the seating admits. §2's bound still holds".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared

feature: **D-0056-2, stored credentials.** "the tool host selects a per-user credential from a store rather than exchanging the round's assertion"; "The host's failure reaches every stored subject, not only the round's. The store becomes part of T-0045-25".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared

feature: **D-0056-3, a request-named subject downstream.** "the downstream system reads the subject from the request (§6)"; "A Thinker's input names the user. The confused deputy is open, and only the bundle and the Observer stand against it".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared

feature: **The confused deputy is closed at three points, each failing toward refusal.** "at grant (no subject without its assertion), at the host (one credential per round) and downstream (§6). Each fails toward refusal."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared
note: The third point is §6's assumption of use, over a system the record excludes as T-0045-39. Finding 5: "The design moves that path to a system TOPAK does not verify, which is the position ⟨U1⟩, and is recorded as one."

feature: **What the record does not cover.** "How a user's request becomes a task"; "Long-running or offline action for a user"; "Delegation between principals, which ADR-0054 decides by seating every cell"; and "A subject's consent, beyond the fact that its provider signed an assertion naming the grant's fence".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared

feature: **The task path is the larger gap (finding 1).** "A round for a user needs a grant that carries the user's assertion. Today grants come from a quorum or an operator", and "A deployment serving users at volume reopens that rate problem. This record binds a subject however the task arrives. It does not say how a user's request arrives."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Open (a task path for end users: "a record of its own")

principle: P9; P10 (Proposed) · strains P9: "nothing labels them so"
feature: **Results from a `subject` call are that user's data, and nothing labels them so (finding 4).** "Within a round one subject holds. Across rounds, a workflow edge (ADR-0054) could carry one user's data into another's round unless the activation is per subject. ADR-0054's pending amendment should say so."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Open (the label of a `subject` call's result; ADR-0054's activation carrying one subject)

feature: **On ratification it closes on-behalf-of attribution for an end user, in one form.** ADR-0037 lists that attribution as not owed; the record takes it "in the one form this record decides (one subject per round, evidenced at grant). Delegation between principals stays as ADR-0054 leaves it."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056: it closes "nothing until ratified")

feature: **Declined: a seat per user, several subjects per round, and leaving the binding to deployments.** A seat per user is rejected because "A user is not promoted and holds no Persona, and a quorum per user does not scale"; several subjects per round "mixes two users' content in one round topic and one `clearSet`"; and having no record is rejected because "The scope can be left to deployments, and §6 does. The binding cannot, because its failure adds authority".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared
note: Also not taken: "A floor forbid on `service` entries in a subject round", since "the floor cannot tell which kind it is (finding 3). The bundle may forbid it".

feature: **The ratification condition names a module, a floor stage and five behaviours to be seen.** A module states at least `SubjectFixedForRound`, `SubjectEvidenced`, `InjectedIsRoundSubject` and `SubjectEntryNeedsSubject`, with mutations `M_INPUT_SUBJECT`, `M_RESUBJECT`, `M_STALE_ASSERTION` and `M_NO_R10`; the reference runs "one `subject` entry over a stub downstream that authorizes by token", with five behaviours, "each seen".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); not built (no module, no `subjects` stage and no ADR-0033 addendum at bbda621); Open (§11, every item)
note: Record against module: there is no module. The four properties and four mutations are names in §11 only; searched across the tree, they occur in ADR-0056 and in the C10 diagram, so nothing can be compared with the record's statements.

feature: **Ratification waits on ADR-0050, and on dependent entries to eight accepted records and the narrative.** "ADR-0050 is confirmed first, or this record is ratified provisionally with it, since it stands on §3 and §5 of that record"; the entries named are to ADR-0049, ADR-0050 §5, ADR-0031 A3, ADR-0041, ADR-0042 §6, ADR-0045, ADR-0025 A2, ADR-0048 §2 and ToO §13, "and ADR-0054 §2 if it is ratified first".
basis: ADR-0056 §11; header (Pending; Carries a debt against)
status: Proposed (ADR-0056; "Pending: none"); Open (§11: "The dependent entries are drafted" is not met)
note: No record it carries a debt against names ADR-0056 at bbda621. Outside itself it is cited by `decisions/README.md`, `diagrams/README.md`, the C10 diagram and two derived proposals of 2026.11.10.

feature: **One author, one day; a reader who is not the drafter is a ratification condition.** The last negative consequence is "One author, one day."; §11 ends with "A reader who is not the drafter (ADR-0029 A2)".
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Open (§11: a reader who is not the drafter)
note: The provenance note says the custodian settled ⟨U1⟩ and ⟨U2⟩ and that every other choice is the drafter's.

feature: **The record answers OWASP LLM06:2025's mitigation 5 and example 5.** "LLM06 mitigation 5 and example 5 have an answer of the pattern's shape. The membrane decides who and whether. The downstream system decides what."
status: Proposed (ADR-0056); Declared
note: One source could not be opened: the provenance note gives the session draft *TOPAK — Position response to OWASP LLM06:2025* as "(2026.11.06, not in the corpus)".

feature: **Confirmation is required under C2 and C4; C1 and C3 are read as not applying.** C2 "because §3 claims that every relation between two specification artifacts the corpus relies on is an edge of the graph, which is an exhaustiveness claim"; C4 "because it makes three open-list items computed rather than found by a reader (G11 items 56, 90 and 103)".
status: Proposed (ADR-0057; C2, C4); Open (the commit that carries the graph; the custodian's reading of findings 7 and 8)
note: Deployment position: "Archetype. A method declaration, as ADR-0046 is: it says how the corpus relates its own artifacts." C3 is set aside "on the drafter's reading", and finding 3 keeps the question for a reviewer.

feature: **Piskala's three levels describe edges, not projects (finding 1).** "The level is a property of the relation between two artifacts, and the corpus has many relations"; placing the project on Piskala's line is rejected because "The corpus sits at five points at once (Context); the level is the edge's".
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Declared

feature: **The corpus already keeps its relations in four places that do not know of each other.** They are `mechanism/corpus-pins.sha256` with `drift.rs`, the binding table and its JSON with `spec/inventory.py`, `manifests/`, and the three sync scripts. Three gaps follow: "A pin says the far end moved, not what the edge was"; "A pin is whole-file, so a History row trips it as a changed clause does"; and a guarantee stated twice "is tied by tests alone, and nothing lists the places where that is so (I47 (e))".
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Declared

feature: **A node is an artifact that states something normative or checks something stated.** "a record's clause, a module, a proof module, a Lean file, a floor stage, a Rego policy, a crate or a function in it, a schema. It is named by its path, and a record's clause by its record and section (§2). Its content is identified by digest."
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Built (419 nodes, counted in the file)
note: §14 itemises the 419 as "283 clauses of 44 records", the 31 modules and 24 proof modules, 14 Lean encodings, `mechanism/lean`'s five files, the genesis floor, its four stages, `floor/lean`, eight crates, the scripts and the reference as a whole. Those sum to 373. The file's other 46 nodes are a whole-record node for each of the 44 records and the binding table's two files. The 283 are 281 clause nodes in the record layer and ADR-0045's two annexes, which the builder puts in the assurance layer. No node is a Rego policy, a function or a schema.

feature: **Layers are open: a layer is a label for reading and carries no premise ⟨K1⟩.** "A new kind of artifact is given a layer name when it first enters the graph, and no record is needed to add one"; the corpus starts with ten: intent, vocabulary, record, assurance, model, interface, policy, implementation, runtime and deployment.
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Built
note: The built graph has nodes in five of the ten. The results file's line reads "intent 0 · vocabulary 0 · record 325 · assurance 4 · model 69 · interface 0 · policy 6 · implementation 15 · runtime 0 · deployment 0". The ToO, the glossary, `policies/`, the recorded traces and a deployment's declaration are not nodes.

feature: **The graph carries no brand name ⟨K3⟩.** "The graph has no name beyond its description, *the specification graph*".
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Declared (the custodian's decision)
note: The summary of the discussion gives the reason: "The obvious name was taken".

feature: **The clause is the binding point above the model layer, and its number is stable.** A clause is "a numbered subsection of a record's Decision, with its inline amendments, cited as the corpus already cites it"; "Records are append-only with typed History rows, so a clause's number is stable. A clause may number its guarantees `§n.k` where it states more than one."
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Built (`spec/clauses.py`, `d476d7659e44d089`)
note: `clauses.py` makes clauses of more than numbered subsections: a record with no Decision section is one clause, `text`; an unnumbered subsection is a clause named by its heading; text before the first subsection is the clause `Decision`; a repeated id takes a suffix. Finding 9(b) records the first two as the drafter's choices. It pins a whole clause and does not split `§n.k` guarantees.

principle: P8.2 · would add the clause's four parts to P8.2
feature: **A record drafted after this one gives each clause four parts: goal, givens, guarantees and discharge.** The goal is "Not normative, and not bound"; the givens are "rows, parameters, derived premises and other clauses, by id"; the fourth part is named *discharge* and not *gate* "because the corpus already has floor gates (ADR-0030 §5) and promotion gates".
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); not built
note: No record at bbda621 has a clause in the four parts, ADR-0059 to ADR-0068 (drafted 2026.11.10, while ADR-0057 was Proposed) included. The one instance is an exercise, `derived/sdd-equivalents-2026.11.06/03-record/topak-clause-ADR-0031-s4-s5.md`. The custodian proposed the name gates; discharge is the drafter's choice.

feature: **Records already ratified are not rewritten.** "Their givens are read from the binding table, which already holds them as each row's premises, and their discharge from the graph. A clause gains the four parts when an amendment next touches it."
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Declared

principle: P8.5 · strains P8.5 ("each mean one thing and are never shortened"): the type *proved* is given to "the graph check of the `Seats`, `FloorComposition` and `Emergency` encodings (T-0045-37)"
feature: **Every edge is typed by what it leaves to a person: eight types, strongest first, in a total order (drafter's choice) ⟨K2⟩.** An edge "runs from a lower node to the node it discharges, and says how"; the types are *executed*, *generated*, *proved*, *proved of a reading*, *replayed*, *tested*, *read* and *trusted*, the last being "Has no edge; a row stands where the edge would be".
status: Proposed (ADR-0057; C2); Built (435 edges, counted by type: *executed* 1, *generated* 4, *proved* 36, *proved of a reading* 20, *replayed* 4, *tested* 9, *read* 340, *trusted* 21); Open (the custodian's reading of the order of §3)
note: The graph's 36 edges of type *proved* are 24 on T-0045-31, 7 on T-0045-37 (four graph-check edges, three from `floor/lean` to floor files) and 5 on T-0045-14, each from a floor file to ADR-0030 §5 on its gates results. §3's table names the first two kinds only and lists "the floor gates' case suites" under *tested*; the graph has no *tested* edge for a case suite. One type word thus covers results for which the list's status key has separate words.

feature: **A citation is not an edge.** "A record citing another, or code citing a record in a comment, discharges nothing; it is how a reader finds the edge."
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Built
note: The builder finds its *read* edges by citation: a module's from the `ADR-NNNN` and `§N` its text cites, the reference's from what its sources cite among the pinned paths, each written with reader "the drafter". The graph therefore has a read edge wherever such a citation is. No edge in the file carries the `reviewed` field that `build` would keep.

feature: **A read edge names its reader, and mutations do not change an edge's type.** "A reading by the drafter and a reading by someone else are the same type, and the graph shows which it was"; mutations and witnesses "show that the module tells the clause from its negation, not that it reads the clause rightly".
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Built (340 read edges, counted: 329 name "the drafter", 11 name no reader yet)
note: The 11 are the `enc-faithful(M)` edges, whose reader field begins "none yet: the premise asks for someone other than the drafter (ADR-0053 §5 R1(b))". No edge names a reader other than the drafter.

feature: **An edge is fresh or stale, and re-pinning is the review.** "It pins the content of both ends, by clause for records (§7) and by digest otherwise. An edge whose pin no longer matches is stale, and is re-pinned by the review `drift.rs` already asks for: read the change, bring the lower node into line or register why not, then re-pin."
status: Proposed (ADR-0057); Built
note: Record against builder, and the record says so in finding 9(a): an edge with no results file whose lower end is the reference or a row "pins its upper end only", since pinning both "would make every commit to the code stale 139 read edges and every trusted edge". That is 160 of the 435 edges (139 read, 21 trusted) pinned at one end where §3 says both.

feature: **Each edge contributes a named premise, and a stale or absent edge's premise is false.** An edge of type *t* from *x* to *y* contributes `edge(t, x → y)`, "a premise column of kind `check` (ADR-0053 R7) whose value is the edge's freshness and, where the type has a results file, that file's verdict"; finding 2: "This record extends a rule; it does not make one."
